title: Talan
dek: The god of Justice and Order holds Death’s forces at bay, kills Aria in their confrontation, and leaves a disputed demand for justice behind him.

facts.Last direct encounter in this review: Leaves the battlefield after killing Aria · 6 Nov 2025
facts.Voraketh: Authorship of the Chains and guardians · attributed account

body:
Talan is a god of Justice and Order in Fenumion’s public record. Aria’s history remembers him through childhood fear, the destruction of his temple and the later confrontation in which he kills her. Her experience of him shapes how she speaks about safety and power.

At Aria’s last battle, his defense against Death’s forces and his killing of Aria become part of the same encounter. The adventurers reach him while already fighting for different reasons. Their presence does not make his claim to justice a judgment they all share.

Holding the line against Death’s forces

On 6 Nov 2025, the expedition reaches a battlefield already deep in war. The narrator describes Talan as the force keeping Death’s army at bay while the opposing divine host is losing. He is bloodied and still fighting, striking down another enemy with his hammer.

Scribonia’s Meteor Swarm destroys most of the remaining Heavenly Host. Talan sounds a horn for reinforcements and holds on. The travelers have entered an existing defense and helped damage it; their attack cannot be described as a simple contest between their company and one isolated god.

Aria sees him and advances with her own history of fear and hatred. Behind the fighting, the ground shakes and reality begins to fade as something approaches. There is little time left for anyone on the battlefield.

The confrontation with Aria

The recorded confrontation on 6 November 2025 ends Aria’s life but does not erase the people, institutions and harm she leaves behind. Talan’s role in that ending connects him to Zarathis’s subsequent memory and political history.

Aria catches Talan’s raised weapon in her hand and meets his gaze. He shouts, “YOU ARE NO GOD.” Their struggle continues, but the narrator makes the difference in their strength clear: Aria is outmatched. A later blow sends her to her knees.

Talan insists that Justice and Law are his very being. This is his declaration during the fight. Aria lies bleeding and crushed while Scribonia also attacks, seeking revenge for what she did to him. Talan’s killing of Aria remains the established outcome; the other adventurer’s participation remains part of how it happened.

The narration ends with Aria small at Talan’s feet and him grinning at a victory in the war. He then leaps into the opening in the Void and leaves the survivors behind. His next destination and later fate are not shown in this encounter.

Justice disputed by the survivors

Olokun calls on Talan to stop the attack on mortals, then turns against him as Aria falls. The objection is voiced within the battle itself. The name of Justice offers no shared answer to the people caught between the forces on the field.

After Talan leaves, Death appears and claims Aria’s body. With a gesture, Death kills the Zarathian troops. Those deaths belong to Death’s action, even though the soldiers have just lost their leader to Talan. Olokun disputes the claim to the body while the Wyrm approaches.

At the later funeral, High Lord Bowene mourns Aria as a mentor and as the best of his people. He demands that Talan pay for killing her. The demand carries grief into public politics; it does not establish that a punishment or later confrontation has occurred.

The full battle account follows the expedition’s divided loyalties, the fight and the dispute over her body. The history of Aria’s tomb follows the procession and the people left to mourn her.

An attributed place in Voraketh

The public Voraketh account attributes the island’s Chains and guardians to Talan through Nuru’s testimony to Anky. This remains an attributed account, not a complete reconstruction of their creation or proof of Talan’s home island.

When Sildithas asks whether the Chains, constructs and unnatural order can all come from one perspective, Anky distinguishes Talan’s work from the other stories being discussed. He says Talan made the Chains and their protectors, then says they keep the Maw at bay.

This report places the same name associated with Aria’s death beside an account of defenses against a dangerous force. It does not settle why those defenses were built, how they now work or whether the people investigating them understand their purpose. The existing Voraketh history keeps those questions open.

Continue reading Aria’s Last Battle · Aria / Pride · Aria’s Tomb · High Lord Bowene · Voraketh

evidence.summary: Aria’s death and Talan’s departure are narrated. Talan’s assertion about his nature remains his assertion; Scribonia’s attack is preserved without replacing the established account of who kills her.

evidence.label: Witnessed quest scenes & attributed accounts
evidence.summary: Actions, objections and funeral speeches are separately attributed. Death kills the troops after Talan leaves. Bowene’s demand is not a completed revenge, and the narrator also preserves Scribonia’s role in the battle.

evidence.label: Attributed report
evidence.summary: Anky reports authorship and purpose; the existing Nuru provenance remains secondhand here. No creation scene, hidden origin, home island, current divine presence or universal metaphysical conclusion is disclosed.

profile.personality: Insists on his own association with Justice and Law during the confrontation with Aria. Her hatred and Olokun’s objection preserve opposing views.
profile.achievements: Holds Death’s forces at bay on the checked battlefield and kills Aria. Later authorship of Voraketh’s Chains is reported by Anky, not witnessed in this selection.
profile.relationships: Aria, Olokun and Bowene meet or remember him through battle and loss; the Voraketh reports retain their separate speakers and limits.
